subtitle: The module that fixes last lesson's comma problem.

code:
import csv

with open("orders.csv", newline="") as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)
    header = next(reader)
    first_row = next(reader)

print(header)
print(first_row)
caption: csv.reader handles quoted fields with embedded commas correctly — every value still comes back as a string.
row["quantity"] beats row[6] for readability — and this is where you actually find orders.csv's two real data problems.

eyebrow: Writing a cleaned CSV with csv.DictWriter
code:
reader = csv.DictReader(f_in)
fieldnames = reader.fieldnames + ["issue"]
writer = csv.DictWriter(f_out, fieldnames=fieldnames)
writer.writeheader()

for row in reader:
    row["issue"] = ""
    if row["customer_name"] == "":
        row["issue"] = "missing_customer_name"
    elif int(row["quantity"]) < 0:
        row["issue"] = "negative_quantity"
    writer.writerow(row)
caption: DictWriter needs an explicit fieldnames list — unlike DictReader, it has no CSV to read column names from.
